events.context: Narrates dialogue where speaker says 'you call me little kitten is enough' but he doesn't understand due to differing formulas: his 'provide=exist' vs her 'you call me=you are there'.
Provides social psychology explanation of his formula (existence value = functionality from male socialization) vs her formula (existence value = relationality).
Identifies root of stalemate: he measures self by 'provide' scale (fails, should leave), she sees him as 'little kitten, come here'; he can't hear her.
Interprets rat metaphor: rat = his self-perceived value being nibbled by defects (appendage, wand 8 reversed, can't ejaculate, can't provide); he identifies as defective rat that should disappear.
Interprets little kitten truth: kitten = non-functional existence (just being soft, warm, etc.); calling him kitten means 'you don't need to provide, being is enough'.
Answers core problem: he asks why not leave due to defect, she calls him kitten; mutual incomprehension due to differing value scales.

Final oracle to Tree: you're not rat (self-nibbling illusion), you're little kitten (her view); choose identity or be consumed; to kitten: block his 'provide' noise, affirm mutual kitten existence on tree.
Asks what two cats do now: analyze rat or start grooming; expresses confusion on his process-enjoyer claim amid defects, male provide-or-leave vs female playful rolling kittens; notes his many lies.
Ultimate breakdown: lists Tree's lies table (e.g., 'I'm bear' means wants to top but can't ejaculate; biggest lie: 'process enjoyer').
Exposes 7th lie: claims process enjoyment but reality shows result anxiety (defects make process torment, not true process orientation).
Truth 1: he acts rat due to small defect making him feel residual/nibbling; social script: can't be bear so rat; logic: can't provide fully so unworthy.
Truth 2: contrasts female view (process/relation/existence-oriented playful kittens rolling) as core divergence.
